options: a link to the relevant lesson section
a full lesson rewrite with exercises

fixed: (1) what it is — three sentences, (2) one worked example from the lesson's own code, (3) one practice item with the answer explained; ≤ two minutes/220 words; concept named; opt-out present; never graded
whatever the model decides fits the learner's level
items.explanation: The format is tested: three parts, the concept named, example from the course's own artifacts, and the word 'graded' banned from the artifact. (obj-20-a)

items.prompt: Where do the message caps (1/day, 3/week, 1 per concept/7 days) live?
options: As constants in the policy, checked BEFORE dispatch, receipted when they fire — changing one is a versioned amendment, not a copy edit
In copy the cohort reads ('we aim for at most one a day')
In the system prompt, so the model can judge each situation
items.explanation: Copy-declared limits drift under product pressure ('this one is important'); code-declared limits hold — and the rate_limited refusal is itself a decision with a receipt, proving restraint. (obj-20-b)

items.prompt: A willing learner was dispatched a micro-lesson on concept X this week and hits the same stuck signal again tomorrow. What happens?
options: Dispatch again — the learner is asking for help
The per-concept cap fires: NO_CHANGE [rate_limited] with a receipt — even eagerness doesn't shift the caps
items.explanation: Caps are checked in consent-then-caps-then-signal order and bind the system itself: a second dispatch this week is a refusal, receipted. (obj-20-b)

items.prompt: What does the dispatch receipt deliberately record about the learner?
options: Only the hashed handle — the receipt is loud about the DECISION (which signal, which caps passed, which concept) and silent about identity
Their name and quiz history for follow-up
items.explanation: If a learner asks 'why did I get this message?', the receipt answers with signal facts without ever naming them to anyone else. (obj-20-a)
